title: Boundary persistence and charged-set repulsion for vertexical differential-inclusion families on all finite hypercubes under opposite-face persistence and charged-vertex repulsion
author: Manoj Gopalkrishnan; Ezra Miller; Anne Shiu
work: A Projection Argument for Differential Inclusions, with Applications to Persistence of Mass-Action Kinetics
source_version: Official SIGMA 9 (2013) article 025, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2013.025; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof combines induction on face dimension with a projection argument in shrinking face blocks, retaining a fixed lower-dimensional inclusion while trajectory time is reparametrized. Its key obligation is to transfer uniform vertex-repulsion neighborhoods back to face repulsion, rather than merely showing that an individual trajectory cannot converge to a corner.

source_check.note: Full original Theorem 3.15 and its complete two-face-claim structural-induction proof are retained with all trajectory, persistence, uniform repulsion, face/block, projection, charged-set and vertexical-family definitions. The index family contains all finite nonempty subsets of positive integers; the repulsing index set may be infinite. Both charged-set repulsion and whole-boundary persistence conclusions remain, with whole-boundary repulsion only under the additional opposite-face repulsion hypothesis. The fixed lower-dimensional differential inclusion and uniform distance estimate, independent of the particular trajectory/subinterval, are supplied; order-preserving continuous time changes remain allowed. Original geometric figures are assets and all proof language/math stays editable. No mass-action application, permanence consequence or deferred strongly-endotactic theorem is selected. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: Read full Theorem3.15 and exact trajectory/persistence/repulsion definitions2.3-2.5, Remarks2.11-2.13, face-block and vertexical definitions3.1-3.14. Index family is all finite nonempty subsets of positive integers; repulsing setR can be infinite. Each member is persistent relative to all opposite faces and repelled by charged vertices. Both conclusions retained: entire-boundary persistence and charged-set repulsion, with whole-boundary repulsion only under the extra opposite-face repulsion assumption. The new proof supplies both face claims and the uniform fixed-Y projection estimate, allowing order-preserving continuous time changes. No mass-action application, permanence consequence, or strongly-endotactic theorem6.11 whose proof is deferred is counted.
